text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel was forced to halt the transport of lorries on Thursday after a problem with the overhead power supply to its trains, a spokeswoman said.
The lorry service resumed only last month on a trial basis following a blaze in the tunnel last November which caused 200 million pounds ($325 million) of damage and injured several people.
One train was trapped in the tunnel for 30 minutes on Thursday morning following the initial power failure, the spokeswoman said.
"We have suspended the service for HGVs (Heavy Goods Vehicles)," she said.
Eurotunnel has been carrying lorries free of charge pending authorisation for a full resumption of freight traffic, which it hopes to receive by mid-June.
The resumption of the service is seen as essential for Eurotunnel, struggling to secure shareholder and bank support for a plan to restructure its $12 billion debt.
The spokeswoman said two trains per hour were running each way through the tunnel while engineers worked on the power supply problem.
Car passengers with prior bookings were being taken through the tunnel but those without reservations were being redirected towards the ferries.
Eurotunnel is awaiting a report from a French investigating magistrate into the causes of the November 18 fire.
Authorisation for the full resumption of freight traffic is dependent on the outcome of a number of safety tests to be completed by June 15. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
